lessons.title: Indices (powers)
lessons.programRef: Cameroon secondary (general education) Mathematics programme, Form 2 (MINESEC) — to be checked against the official programme
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Write repeated multiplication as a power
Use the laws of indices for multiplying, dividing and raising to a power
Use the zero and negative indices
reviewNotes: Fractional indices are left for Form 3; the official scheme may introduce them earlier.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Index notation
blocks.md: In $a^n$, a is the **base** and n is the **index** (power or exponent): $2^5 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 32$. $a^2$ is 'a squared' and $a^3$ is 'a cubed'.

blocks.title: Laws of indices
blocks.md:
- $a^m \times a^n = a^{m+n}$
- $a^m \div a^n = a^{m-n}$
- $(a^m)^n = a^{mn}$
- $a^0 = 1$ (for a not zero)
- $a^{-n} = \frac{1}{a^n}$
- $(ab)^n = a^n b^n$
The first two laws need the **same base**.

blocks.title: Method with algebra
blocks.md: Multiply the numbers in front, and add the indices of the same letter: $2x^3 \times 3x^4 = 6x^7$. For a bracket with a power, raise every factor: $(2a^2)^3 = 2^3 a^6 = 8a^6$. Divide the numbers and subtract the indices: $12x^5 \div 4x^2 = 3x^3$.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- $2^3 \times 2^4$ is $2^7$, not $4^7$: the base stays the same.
- $(2a)^3$ is $8a^3$, not $2a^3$.
- $a^{-2}$ is $\frac{1}{a^2}$, not a negative number; and $a^0$ is 1, not 0.

lessons.title: Approximation and standard form
lessons.programRef: Cameroon secondary (general education) Mathematics programme, Form 2 (MINESEC) — to be checked against the official programme
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Round to a number of decimal places and significant figures
Write large and small numbers in standard form
Calculate with numbers in standard form
reviewNotes: Check how many significant figures the official scheme expects in Form 2.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Rounding
blocks.md: To round to **n decimal places**, keep n digits after the decimal point and look at the next digit. To round to **n significant figures** (s.f.), count from the first non-zero digit. Examples: 3.456 → 3.5 (1 d.p.); 0.004567 → 0.0046 (2 s.f.); 45 678 → 45 700 (3 s.f.). Zeros that only show the size of the number are filled in.

blocks.title: Standard form
blocks.md: A number is in **standard form** when it is written $a \times 10^n$ with $1 \leq a < 10$ and n an integer. Large numbers have a positive n: $4\,500\,000 = 4.5 \times 10^6$. Small numbers have a negative n: $0.00032 = 3.2 \times 10^{-4}$.

blocks.title: Calculating
blocks.md: To multiply, multiply the numbers a and add the indices; to divide, divide the numbers and subtract the indices. Then adjust to standard form. $(2 \times 10^3) \times (3 \times 10^4) = 6 \times 10^7$. $(8 \times 10^5) \times (5 \times 10^2) = 40 \times 10^7 = 4 \times 10^8$.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Writing 45 × 10⁵ in standard form: a must be between 1 and 10, so it is 4.5 × 10⁶.
- Counting zeros as significant when they only hold place value.
- Using a positive index for a small number: 0.003 is 3 × 10⁻³.

blocks.title: Example 1: write in standard form
blocks.statement: Write 45 000 and 0.0032 in standard form. Round 0.004567 to 2 s.f.
steps: 45 000: move the decimal point 4 places left, so 4.5 × 10⁴.
0.004567: the first non-zero digit is 4; two s.f. gives 0.0046 (next digit 5 rounds up).

blocks.title: Example 2: calculation
blocks.statement: A store at Douala port holds 3.6 × 10⁵ kg of cocoa in sacks of 6 × 10¹ kg each. Find the number of sacks.

lessons.title: Speed, distance, time and rates

lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Use the relation between speed, distance and time
Calculate average speed for a whole journey
reviewNotes: The Bamenda trip figures are made up for practice; they are not real route data.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Speed, distance and time
blocks.md: Speed measures how fast something moves. For constant speed:

blocks.title: Average speed
blocks.md: **Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.** The total time includes stops. Convert times to hours: 45 minutes = 0.75 h and 2 h 30 min = 2.5 h. To change km/h into m/s multiply by 1 000 and divide by 3 600 (that is divide by 3.6): 72 km/h = 20 m/s.

blocks.title: Distance-time graphs
blocks.md: On a distance-time graph the **gradient** is the speed. A rising line means moving away; a **horizontal** line means stopped; a falling line means coming back. A steeper line means a faster speed.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Writing 2 h 30 min as 2.30 h: it is 2.5 h.
- Averaging two speeds instead of dividing total distance by total time.
- Forgetting the rest time in the total time of the journey.

blocks.title: Example 1: average speed
blocks.statement: A bus leaves Bamenda, travels 120 km in 2 hours, rests for 30 minutes and then returns the 120 km in 2 hours (see the graph). Find its speed on the way out and its average speed for the whole trip.
steps: Total time = 2 + 0.5 + 2 = 4.5 h, so average speed = 240 ÷ 4.5 ≈ 53.3 km/h.

blocks.title: Example 2: conversion and time
blocks.statement: Convert 72 km/h to m/s. A cyclist covers 18 km in 45 minutes: find the speed in km/h.

objectives: Calculate profit and loss and express them as percentages
Find the selling price after a discount
reviewNotes: Compound interest, VAT and hire purchase are left for Form 3.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Profit and loss
blocks.md: Profit = selling price (SP) − cost price (CP). Loss = CP − SP. Percentages are always taken on the **cost price**:

blocks.title: Discount and commission
blocks.md: A **discount** is a reduction of the marked price: selling price = marked price × $(1 - \frac{d}{100})$. **Commission** is a percentage of the sales paid to an agent. A shop marked a phone at 25 000 FCFA with 12% off: 25 000 × 0.88 = 22 000 FCFA.

blocks.title: Simple interest
blocks.md: Interest earned or paid on the **original** amount only. P = principal, R = rate per year (%), T = time in years:

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Calculating profit % on the selling price instead of the cost price.
- Forgetting that the amount after interest is **principal + interest**.
- Using months for T: change to years (6 months = 0.5 year).

blocks.title: Example 1: profit and loss
blocks.statement: A trader in Bafoussam buys a bag of beans for 15 000 FCFA and sells it for 18 000 FCFA. Find the profit percent. Another bag costs 40 000 FCFA and is sold for 34 000 FCFA: find the loss percent.

blocks.title: Example 2: interest and discount
blocks.statement: A woman saves 200 000 FCFA at 6% simple interest per year for 3 years. Find the interest and the total. A shirt marked 25 000 FCFA is sold with 12% off: find the price.
steps: Discount = 12% of 25 000 = 3 000, so the price is 22 000 FCFA (also 25 000 × 0.88).
